mount_text.submodule_not_git: {{root}} is not a git repository — mode 'submodule' needs one. Run `git init` first, or attach with `--mode vendored`.
mount_text.submodule_not_recorded:
{{relative}} exists but git does not record it as a submodule — it is {{what}}. `init` will not delete a tree it did not create, and the removal is a commit of yours (D5). Remove it, then re-run:
{{removal}}
mount_text.submodule_what_mounted: an akmon tree mounted some other way (vendored or subtree)
mount_text.submodule_add_failed: git submodule add failed ({{code}}); see the git output above
mount_text.submodule_bump_step: review the pin bump and stage it yourself — `git add -- {{relative}}` (D5: the pin bump and its commit are the owner's; read the CHANGELOG window between the two versions first)
mount_text.submodule_no_release: {{relative}} carries no release tag; left at the default branch
mount_text.submodule_left: {{relative}} left at its current pin (pass --ref to move it)
mount_text.subtree_not_git: {{root}} is not a git repository — mode 'subtree' needs one (or use `--mode vendored`).
mount_text.subtree_is_submodule:
git records {{relative}} as a submodule, not a subtree. Retire it first, then add the subtree:
{{removal}}
mount_text.subtree_needs_ref: mode 'subtree': pass `--ref <tag>` naming the ref merged into {{relative}}. A subtree keeps no git metadata of its own, so the recorded pin can only come from you.
mount_text.subtree_realigning: {{relative}} is already mounted as a subtree — realigning at {{ref}} (bump it with `git subtree pull`)
mount_text.vendored_ref: mode 'vendored' copies the embedded tree of the installed akmon package, so its pin is that package's version ({{version}}) and `--ref {{ref}}` cannot change it. Pin a ref with `--mode submodule`/`--mode subtree`, or install the akmon version you want to vendor.
mount_text.vendored_into_submodule:
git records {{relative}} as a submodule; vendoring into it would leave the consumer with a gitlink over hand-copied files. Retire the submodule first, then re-run:
{{removal}}
mount_text.vendored_foreign: {{relative}} exists and is not an akmon tree — refusing to copy over it; remove it or pick another --aitna-root
mount_text.vendored_in_place: {{relative}} is the tree this CLI runs from — nothing to copy (pin: {{version}})
mount_text.ref_unreachable: cannot discover the latest release tag from {{repo}} (`git ls-remote` needs git and network access to it); pass --ref explicitly
mount_text.ref_no_release: repository {{repo}} advertises no release tags; pass --ref explicitly
mount_text.switch_needs_flag: this project is attached in mount mode {{previous}}; {{mode}} is a **migration**, not a realign — the AGENTS.md akmon block still points at the old layout and the old mount is still on disk, so finishing silently would leave `{{cli}} verify --strict` red. Re-run with `--switch-mode` and init will attach in the new mode and print the edits it must not make for you.

agents_header:
# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot) working in this
repository. Vendor pointer files import this document — it is the single source of truth.
agents_block:
{{heading}} (developing the project)

This project uses the akmon dev layer — one standard for how an assistant helps develop it.
Model & notation: [`MODEL.md`]({{model}}); attach/realign guide:
[`BOOTSTRAP.md`]({{bootstrap}}); overview: [`README.md`]({{readme}}).

- **Archetype / language:** `{{archetype}}` / `{{language}}` — classify per
  [`ARCHETYPES.md`]({{archetypes}}), then update this line, the guardrail imports
  below, and `attached_archetype` in `{{aitna}}/.akmon.toml`.
- **Layers:** SHARED = {{shared_layer}} · LOCAL = `{{aitna}}/{agents,skills,tools,memory}` +
  [`{{aitna}}/TASKS.md`]({{aitna}}/TASKS.md) · USAGE = root `skills/` (absent until this project
  exposes one).
- **Agents (roles):** [review]({{aitna}}/agents/review/README.md),
  [architect]({{aitna}}/agents/architect/README.md), [engineer]({{aitna}}/agents/engineer/README.md)
  → {{roles_hint}}.
  **Declare the active agent** before doing work and restate it on switch
  (`🧭 agent: <name> — <focus>`).
- **Delegation (always-on, direct):** **delegation is the default.** For every non-trivial
  task, before the first repository sweep, edit, or test run, decompose the work and delegate
  every independent mechanical sub-step to available subagents without waiting for an owner
  prompt. The orchestrator retains decomposition, routing, synthesis, and owner dialogue. Skip
  only when the task is atomic or the harness exposes no subagents; state the reason. This
  clause is direct because Codex does not expand nested `@` imports in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Owner authority (always-on — it overrides any task instruction):** the owner verifies
  consequential architecture, data-shape and math decisions recorded in ADRs; an assistant
  *drafts*, the owner *decides*. **D5** — the owner owns commits, tags, pushes, publishing and pin bumps; never
  `git add`/`commit`/`push` on the owner's behalf.
- **Guardrails and profiles (always-on):** the common guardrail and the project's language
  profiles are **imported** (not just linked) so their rules load at session start; akmon is the
  single owner — do not restate them here. One import per line below: `init` writes one per
  language it detected; add any other (`@{{profiles_dir}}/<name>.md`), and an environment
  profile where some of the code runs in one, per the ARCHETYPES map.

@{{guardrails_dir}}/_common.md{{profile_imports}}

- **Domain profiles (opt-in by need):** none attached yet — link only those the project actually needs.
- **Pipelines:** [pre-commit]({{pre_commit}}) (tests mandatory),
  [review-flow]({{review_flow}}),
  [design-flow]({{design_flow}}),
  [code-flow]({{code_flow}}),
  [tasks]({{tasks_link}}) (backlog format), and the learn loop
  ([memory-distill]({{memory_distill}}) +
  [learning]({{learning}})).
- **Memory:** read `{{aitna}}/memory/` at session start — distilled project facts, indexed by
  [`{{aitna}}/memory/README.md`]({{aitna}}/memory/README.md).
- **Backlog:** [`{{aitna}}/TASKS.md`]({{aitna}}/TASKS.md) — one line per task, detail by reference;
  finished entries move to `TASKS_ARCHIVE.md`.
- **Secrets:** from `.env` (gitignored). Never in code, docs, tests, or commits.
agents_roles_hint_package: roles: [`akmon/roles/`]({{roles_link}}) — run `akmon path` to read them locally
agents_shared_layer_package: installed `akmon` package (hooks and tools run from it via `akmon hook`; only the imported guardrails and profiles are materialized, under `{{aitna}}/.akmon/`; `akmon path` locates the rest)
tasks_skeleton:
# TASKS — project backlog

The single backlog for this project. **Index, not a document:** one line per task, detail by
reference; a finished entry moves to `TASKS_ARCHIVE.md`. No dates — git history is the
timeline. Format (akmon `pipelines/tasks.md`):

`- <id> · <title> · <status> · <goal, 12 words max> · [detail](link)`

The id is typed — `A` architecture · `C` code · `N` analysis · `L` learning · `V` release —
and the owning role follows from that letter, so it is not a separate field. Status is one of
`active | blocked | deferred | done`.

- A1 · classify archetype and language · active · pick archetype/language per ARCHETYPES.md; import its language profile
- C1 · pin the test runner · active · record `[test].runner` in `{{aitna}}/.akmon.toml`, reusing this project's manager
memory_index:
# Project memory

Distilled, durable facts about this project — read at session start. One file per fact,
listed here; the learn loop (akmon `pipelines/memory-distill.md`) writes them.

<!-- - [example-fact](example-fact.md) — one-line hook -->

charters.review: assess what *is* — architecture, risk, trade-offs, conformance; a findings report
charters.architect: design what *should be* — options, contracts, docs, decision records
charters.engineer: realize a decided structure in code, with tests

charter_locate_package: `akmon path` prints the standard's root; a mounted consumer reads `{{aitna}}/akmon/roles/{{role}}.md`.

mode_switch_step: re-point the AGENTS.md akmon block from the {{previous}} layout to {{mode}}: the imports become `@{{base}}/guardrails/_common.md` plus each imported profile (`@{{base}}/profiles/<name>.md`), and every link to the standard's docs {{link_resolution}}
mode_switch_link_resolution_package: becomes a GitHub link at the pinned tag, with `akmon path` named as the way to read them locally
mode_switch_remove_mount: remove the now-unused mount `{{aitna}}/akmon` (`git rm -r --cached` + `rm -rf`, or `git submodule deinit` first if it was a submodule) — nothing reads it in package mode

pin_step.none: **pin akmon in the project's dependency manifest**, in a **dev** group (never a runtime dependency): "akmon @ git+{{repo}}@{{ref}}" — then install it into a virtualenv inside the project root. Until both are done, `akmon` cannot resolve here: the CI checks cannot run, and the generated hook commands fail silently because the console script they name does not exist
pin_step.runtime: **move the akmon pin** out of the project's runtime dependencies (or extras) into a **dev** group: akmon is dev tooling and must not reach this project's own users (ADR 0009 §4)
pin_step.unreadable: **fix pyproject.toml** — it is not valid TOML, so neither akmon nor uv can read an akmon pin from it; once it parses, the pin belongs in a **dev** group

ruff_step.uv: add ruff as a development dependency so `akmon check` can run it: `uv add --dev ruff`
ruff_step.poetry: add ruff as a development dependency so `akmon check` can run it: `poetry add --group dev ruff`
ruff_step.none: add ruff to the project's development dependencies so `akmon check` can run it

checks_redecided_empty: [check] records no checks and --checks was given — deciding it again

report.complete: attached, with steps left to a human/agent decision:

missing.unreadable: cannot read an akmon pin: pyproject.toml is not valid TOML (step 1)
missing.absent: has no akmon pin in a dev group yet (step 1) — nothing else attaches it

report.exit: exit 1: mode 'package' {{missing}}, so this attach is not finished. Re-run `akmon init` after {{remedy}} (it keeps the recorded mode), or `akmon verify --strict` to re-check.

closing_steps.classify: classify the project (archetype + language) against ARCHETYPES.md, import the language profile in AGENTS.md, and set `attached_archetype` in {{aitna}}/.akmon.toml
closing_steps.classify_archetype: classify the project's archetype against ARCHETYPES.md and set `attached_archetype` in {{aitna}}/.akmon.toml
closing_steps.pin_test: pin the test environment: record the project's own pytest invocation as `[test].runner` in {{aitna}}/.akmon.toml (BOOTSTRAP §A5 — do not build a venv when the project already has one)
closing_steps.pin_test_node: pin the test environment: record the project's own test command (`{{test}}`, for example) as `[test].runner` in {{aitna}}/.akmon.toml (BOOTSTRAP §A5)
closing_steps.export_aitna: export AITNA_ROOT={{aitna}} in every shell and CI job that runs the akmon tooling
closing_steps.verify_node: run `{{exec}}akmon verify --strict` and review the diff — the owner commits, not the assistant (D5)
closing_steps.verify_node_mounted: run `{{cli}} verify --strict` and review the diff — the owner commits, not the assistant (D5)
closing_steps.node_mounted_script: optional: name the mounted CLI in package.json `scripts` (`"akmon": "{{cli}}"`, then `{{run_script}} akmon -- verify --strict`); init does not edit package.json
closing_steps.node_no_ruff: this project has package.json and no Python files, so no ruff was set up: name the project's own JavaScript checks under `[check]` in {{record}}
closing_steps.node_no_ruff_mounted: this project has package.json and no Python files, so no ruff was set up: name the project's own JavaScript checks under `[check]` in {{record}}, or move this mount to the JavaScript implementation of akmon, which needs no Python, with `{{switch}}`, then have it detect them with `{{detect}}` (a first attach of a Node repository is `{{attach}}`)
closing_steps.verify: run `akmon verify --strict` and review the diff — the owner commits, not the assistant (D5)
